entry.title: Why Image Hallucination Is More Dangerous Than Text Hallucination
entry.summary: We’ve spent a lot of time talking about text hallucinations. In vision-language systems, hallucination isn’t about plausible lies. Examples: Describing people who aren’t there Assigning attributes that don’t exist Inferring actions that never happened As these models are deployed for: E-commerce product listings …the cost of hallucination changes from “wrong answer” to “real-world consequence.” The issue is that most evaluation pipelines are still text-first. Image hallucination requires multimodal evaluation: Compare generated text against visual evidence Reason about object presence, attributes, and relationships Detect contradictions between image and output This isn’t a niche problem. Curious how others are approaching hallucination detection for image-based systems.
